title: TeklaDump inspect document 1.0
description: A curated view of a handful of Tekla model objects. Generated from the extractors' declared keys; do not hand-edit.

point.description: A point in the CURRENT work plane of the session the dump was taken in. See the header's workPlane field.

reference.description: A related object, named and never followed. The GUID identifies an object in the SOURCE model; it means nothing in a model the generated code runs against.

templateValue.description: A template (report) value. A bare number is in the units the header declares. The object form appears only for an attribute whose unit is known but not normalizable.

header.description: Self-describing preamble; line 1 of a bulk file.

modelPath.description: Only when IncludeSessionDetails is on. Off by default: an inspect file is meant to be pasted into a chat.

user.description: The Tekla user, not the Windows account. Session-details gated.

numberingUpToDate.description: False means position and mark attributes are empty or stale. There is no API to run numbering.

objectCount.description: Present only when the count was known before writing started.

objectType.description: The CLR simple name of the Tekla type.

guid.description: Stable identity. Absent for an uninserted object, which has none.

create.description: Properties that can be assigned when recreating the object. A starting point for code you write, not an importer payload.

derived.description: Strictly informational. Assigning any of these is either impossible or a mistake.

componentAttributes.description: Component attributes the user actually SET. An attribute the user never set is omitted, because the component is using its own default.

Phase.description: Phase number the object belongs to.

FatherComponent.description: The component that created this object, when one did. Its presence is the warning that editing this object by hand will be undone the next time the component regenerates.

Class.description: Class. A string in the API even though it looks like a number.

Finish.description: Finish, e.g. a paint or galvanising code.

Position.description: Depth / Plane / Rotation enum names and their three offsets. The part of a part that is hardest to reproduce from a screenshot.

AssemblyNumber.description: Assembly numbering series: Prefix and StartNumber.

Assembly.description: The assembly this part belongs to.

Solid.description: Bounding box of the computed solid. Only when Geometry = Solids — computing it is orders of magnitude more expensive than every other field combined.
